movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
Assault Vest-boosted mixed bulk and a strong offensive and defensive typing render Okidogi a potent bulky attacker able to make considerable progress throughout the game with the combination of Knock Off and Toxic Chain. Defensively, resistances to Dark and Fighting and a neutrality to Fairy let Okidogi respond to Pokemon like Zamazenta, Darkrai, and Iron Valiant and find ample opportunities to begin forcing progress. Offensively, Okidogi's Poison typing heavily discourages Fairy-types like Clefable and Primarina from attempting to absorb Knock Off, while its Fighting-type STAB move makes it especially threatening to certain poison-immune foes like Kingambit and Garganacl that can avoid Toxic Chain. Knock Off both removes items from switch-ins like Moltres and Great Tusk and rounds out Okidogi's coverage against would-be checks like Gholdengo, Pecharunt, and Galarian Slowking. Lastly, Ice Punch provides valuable coverage against checks like Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Dragonite. 16 Speed EVs let Okidogi outspeed Adamant Kingambit and Ursaluna, letting it serve as a secondary check to them. Tera Water is a robust defensive typing that lets Okidogi shed its Ground- and Psychic-type weaknesses to become a more effective check to Enamorus and Hatterene while improving its matchup into wallbreakers like Walking Wake and Primarina. Alternatively, Tera Dark flips Okidogi's Psychic weakness into an immunity, turning the tables on Gholdengo and Iron Valiant carrying Psyshock, and confers a Ghost resistance alongside STAB on Knock Off to more strongly threaten Pecharunt and Gholdengo.

Assault Vest Okidogi slots comfortably into balance teams in need of a strong progress-maker able to sponge hits from offensive threats like Iron Valiant and Darkrai and punch holes into common physical walls like Zapdos, Zamazenta, and Moltres. Okidogi is highly vulnerable to entry hazard damage, as it repeatedly enters the field to force progress, and it thus greatly appreciates the hazard removal provided by Great Tusk. Okidogi answers fast threats like Iron Valiant and Zamazenta that scare Great Tusk out, while Great Tusk is able to provide more consistent hazard removal with less fear of Moltres and Pecharunt, helping Okidogi maintain its longevity. Ting-Lu is a synergistic defensive teammate that answers threats like Iron Moth and Iron Crown that trouble Okidogi. Beyond handling Fighting- and Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Zamazenta that scare out Ting-Lu, both work together to hold off threats like Darkrai and Gholdengo, and Ting-Lu's ability to set entry hazards greatly complements Okidogi's ease of removing items. This greatly enables powerful teammates like Ogerpon-W, which shreds through checks to Okidogi like Great Tusk and Corviknight in return. Likewise, Dragonite provides a switch-in to threatening Ground-types like Landorus-T and Gliscor and easily picks off weakened teams with Extreme Speed. Kingambit is another brutal endgame cleaner that scares out Psychic-types like Iron Crown and Latios that threaten Okidogi and greatly appreciates their shared checks being weakened.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
Okidogi takes on top-tier threats such as Zamazenta, Darkrai, and Kingambit while becoming a scary offensive threat with Bulk Up and Drain Punch to keep itself healthy. It can also take on other Iron Defense users such as Corviknight and Garganacl. Knock Off removes items from switch-ins such as Zapdos and Moltres, which threaten it immensely, while also hitting Gholdengo for big damage. Ice Punch hits Gliscor and Landorus-T, which could otherwise trade with it. Guard Dog allows Okidogi to ignore Roar from Zamazenta, Whirlwind from Ting-Lu, and Red Card from Glimmora while also giving it an Attack boost from Landorus-T's Intimidate, meaning that it cannot be weakened by Intimidate from frequent switch-ins. 96 Speed EVs let Okidogi outspeed Modest Primarina and Jolly Kingambit, with the rest being put into HP and Special Defense to help Okidogi take on Pokemon such as Darkrai and Iron Valiant a lot more easily. Tera Water allows Okidogi to take hits from Ogerpon-W and Walking Wake effectively, and it removes Okidogi's Ground weakness to allow it to take on Great Tusk and Gliscor while being a generally good Tera type.

Okidogi fits best on bulky offense and balance teams where it can help wall a large proportion of the metagame while outputting offensive pressure. Kingambit is a great partner to Okidogi, as Okidogi can take on the Fighting-types that it struggles against, such as Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, while Kingambit takes on the Psychic-types that scare out Okidogi, such as Galarian Slowking and Latios. Together, they can also overwhelm Pokemon that check them, such as Landorus-T and Great Tusk. Specially defensive pivots such as Galarian Slowking and Iron Crown can switch into the special attackers that threaten Okidogi, such as Zapdos and Raging Bolt. In return, Okidogi can utilize their pivoting options in order to take on Pokemon that they may struggle with, such as Kingambit and Dragonite. Physical attackers such as Dragonite and Ogerpon-W pair well with Okidogi, as they appreciate it wearing down physical walls with Knock Off while taking on Pokemon like Zamazenta or Corviknight that they may struggle with. Spikes setters such as Ting-Lu and Hisuian Samurott pair well with Okidogi, as they can help Okidogi wear down its checks, such as Gholdengo and Great Tusk, with chip damage. They can also check Pokemon such as Gholdengo that Okidogi may struggle more against. In return, Okidogi takes on Fighting-types such as Iron Valiant and Zamazenta, which they may struggle with, while also taking on Corviknight, which can clear away their Spikes with Defog.

strategies.overview:
Fighting

Okidogi is appealing, (AC) as its high natural bulk and helpful Poison typing make it a strong deterrent against Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant compared to Sneasler, which struggles to come in. Additionally, Okidogi takes on Ghost-types much better thanks to its access to Knock Off. However, Sneasler's incredible Speed tier gets the jump on the aforementioned Fairy-types, while Okidogi has to usually endure double the hits, and it doesn't help Okidogi if foes like Hatterene decide to OHKO it with Psyshock. Iron Hands also serves as incredible competition in both roles Okidogi wants to play, thanks to its superior natural bulk and valuable ability to handle Flying-types, which most other teammates completely crumble to.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Poison (Bulk Up)

Ice Punch can be run over Substitute or Taunt, enabling Okidogi to handle Landorus formes on a predicted switch along with helping handle Gliscor and Clodsire, which can otherwise be annoying for it to take on with just Knock Off. However, this comes at the cost of extremely valuable utility, preventing Okidogi from shutting down attempts to stop it with the likes of Haze Toxapex with Taunt or avoid status from the likes of Archaludon or Moltres coming in with Substitute. Toxic Chain can be used over Guard Dog to enable Okidogi to put pressure onto otherwise infuriating walls like Sableye, Great Tusk, and Hippowdon, which can otherwise handle Okidogi with ease. However, it removes Okidogi's ability to beat Skarmory while maintaining a Substitute and avoid phazing from Dragon Tail Gyarados when running Taunt sets.

movesets.name: Bulk Up (Poison)
movesets.description:
With its incredible natural bulk and invaluable secondary Fighting typing, Okidogi serves as an incredible Bulk Up sweeper for Poison teams, enabling them to have a fighting chance against the likes of Dark and Steel. Drain Punch is used to provide Okidogi with long-term sustain and check the likes of Bisharp and Hisuian Goodra comfortably. Knock Off threatens Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo, Hisuian Zoroark, and Galarian Slowking along with removing crucial held items like Skarmory's Rocky Helmet and Toxapex's Black Sludge. Finally, Okidogi has two valuable utility options, with Substitute being the preferred one, as it can be used against foes Okidogi forces out like Hisuian Goodra and Blissey. This lets Okidogi scout incoming switches from the likes of Latios and Hisuian Zoroark along with helping deny Scald burns from Alomomola, Salt Cure from Garganacl, and Thunder Wave from Gholdengo and Archaludon. Alternatively, Taunt can be used to exploit the likes of Skarmory and Toxapex, turning otherwise infuriating checks into setup fodder.

Alolan Muk is a vital teammate, with its Dark typing helping it threaten Psychic- and Ghost-types that cause significant headaches for Okidogi like Deoxys-S, Hatterene, and Spectrier along with letting it answer special attackers that would devastate Okidogi such as Psychic Noise Primarina and Psychic Volcarona. Assault Vest Galarian Slowking can help wear down the likes of Zapdos, Latios, and Pelipper with its strong movepool; it can also use Future Sight to help pressure Poison-type walls such as Toxapex and Pecharunt, which can effortlessly handle Okidogi otherwise. Amoonguss acts as a comfortable check to the likes of Ogerpon-W, Urshifu-R, and Great Tusk along with being able to use Spore to give Okidogi free turns to set up with Bulk Up. Galarian Weezing can use Defog to clear entry hazards and use Will-O-Wisp to weaken physical attackers such as Hippowdon and Ogerpon-C, enabling Okidogi to come in on greatly weakened attacks and easily set up. Iron Moth serves as a fantastic offensive complement to Okidogi, as it can easily remove the likes of Gholdengo and Excadrill with its STAB Flamethrower as well as Pelipper and Great Tusk with its strong coverage in Discharge and Energy Ball, eliminating key problems for Okidogi. Okidogi, in return, is able to pressure special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Ting-Lu with Drain Punch. Pecharunt can provide a strong blanket physical check to the likes of Ogerpon-H and Iron Hands along with being able to pivot Okidogi in with Parting Shot. Alternatively, Nasty Plot Pecharunt can help wear down problematic checks like Gliscor and Galarian Weezing. Salazzle and Glimmora can provide Corrosion Toxic support to wear down opposing walls such as Corviknight, Toxapex, and Pecharunt, greatly limiting their ability to check Okidogi. Salazzle and Glimmora can also provide further support, as Salazzle can use Flamethrower to pressure Gholdengo and Encore to lock foes like Bisharp and Lokix into Sucker Punch, enabling Okidogi to enter the field safely and remove them with Drain Punch for recovery. Glimmora, meanwhile, can use Stealth Rock and Power Gem to pressure Flying-types like Tornadus-T and Dragonite, greatly limiting their ability to come in on Okidogi.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Poison)
movesets.description:
With a Choice Scarf, Okidogi becomes a surprising threat on Poison teams, leveraging its immense coverage movepool and superior bulk over its competition in Sneasler to check dangerous targets like Landorus and Spectrier. Close Combat targets common Dark- and Steel-type threats such as Hydreigon, Bisharp, and Heatran. Knock Off threatens Ghost- and Psychic-type threats like Dragapult, Spectrier, and Latios that would switch into Close Combat along with providing item removal. Ice Punch OHKOes Landorus, an immense issue for Poison, along with other Flying-type foes such as Dragonite and Gliscor. Gunk Shot provides a strong secondary STAB move that can remove targets including Ogerpon-H, Flutter Mane, and Iron Valiant. Alternatively, High Horsepower can be used to deal with opposing Poison-types like Clodsire, Sneasler, and Iron Moth.

Iron Moth forms a solid offensive core with Okidogi, removing physical walls such as Galarian Weezing, Corviknight, Skarmory, and Forretress while appreciating Okidogi's ability to remove special walls like Clodsire, Heatran, and Blissey. Glimmora, Overqwil, and Clodsire all provide support by laying entry hazards to chip down threats like Toxapex, Dragapult, and Gholdengo. Glimmora continues to support Okidogi by threatening problematic Flying-types like Moltres and Zapdos along with spreading Corrosion Toxic to chip down physical walls like Galarian Weezing and Pecharunt. Overqwil deals with physical Psychic- and Ghost-types like Iron Boulder, Gallade, and Ceruledge. Clodsire deals with Fire-type threats like Volcarona and Iron Moth. Galarian Weezing, thanks to Levitate, provides immense support with Defog to remove entry hazards to give Okidogi safe entry along with handling threats such as Great Tusk, Sableye, and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon that threaten Okidogi immensely. Galarian Weezing can also use Will-O-Wisp to both chip down targets and give Okidogi safe entry against weakened physical attackers. Amoonguss helps deal with Ground- and Water-type foes including Great Tusk, Swampert, and Urshifu-R along with providing safe entry with Spore. Toxapex provides a solid way to deal with threats like Scizor that can threaten Okidogi with priority along with handling Araquanid. Alolan Muk handles powerful special attackers like Espathra, Latias, and Hisuian Zoroark along with removing Choice Scarf from the likes of Gholdengo and Hoopa-U thanks to Knock Off.

movesets.name: Assault Vest (Fighting)
movesets.description:
16 Speed EVs lets it outspeed Azumarill. Gunk Shot lets Okidogi deal with Flutter Mane.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description: Okidogi's Speed investment lets it outspeed Dragapult and Adamant Choice Scarf Landorus-T in Tailwind.

strategies.overview:
• Okidogi's main role is to stay on the field to deal consistent damage and pressure common Pokemon like Incineroar and Rillaboom. Okidogi uses its Guard Dog ability to punish any Pokemon with the Intimidate ability, such as Incineroar and Hisuian Arcanine, that switch in. Thanks to its Poison typing, Okidogi can take on Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Tera Fairy Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Raging Bolt.

  • Okidogi is best on teams where it can utilize its bulk and utility, such as balance or bulky offense. Grimmsnarl gives Okidogi dual screens and Thunder Wave support. Thunder Wave allows Okidogi to outspeed the Ogerpon formes. Galarian Moltres can give Okidogi spread Dark-type damage in Fiery Wrath to hit Gholdengo. Roaring Moon acts as a switch-in to Expanding Force from foes like Iron Crown, threatening huge damage with Knock Off and providing Okidogi with Tailwind to patch up its mediocre Speed. Okidogi helps Roaring Moon in return by beating Flutter Mane, Raging Bolt, and Incineroar. Ogerpon-W helps defeat Landorus, while Okidogi can help Ogerpon-W by beating Raging Bolt, Rillaboom, and Urshifu.

  • Because of Okidogi's poor defensive typing, it struggles to take on Pokemon such as Landorus, Landorus-T, Iron Crown, and Tornadus. Okidogi isn't that bulky, meaning it cannot trade damage that well. This means that Okidogi needs dual screens support to do so better.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description:
• Assault Vest Okidogi is a bulky Pokemon capable of trading damage and acting as a deterrent to Intimidate thanks to Guard Dog. Okidogi is primarily used to punish Fake Out users like Incineroar and Rillaboom.

  • Gunk Shot is Okidogi's primary Poison-type STAB move, notably securing an OHKO on Rillaboom, bulky Ogerpon-W and Ogerpon-H, and frailer Flutter Mane variants while securing a 2HKO on Bold Flutter Mane. Poison Jab is also usable, trading damage for consistent accuracy. Upper Hand pressures the opponent to not use any priority moves while Okidogi is on the field; this is notably useful against Fake Out users. Okidogi struggles to damage Gholdengo and Landorus with its STAB combination, forcing it to run coverage moves. However, it can only fit one coverage move, so it must choose between a move to deal with Gholdengo and a move to deal with Landorus. Knock Off notably deals super effective damage to Gholdengo, Indeedee-F, and Iron Crown; Ice Punch is coverage for Landorus. High Horsepower maintains Okidogi's ability to hit Gholdengo and Iron Crown while also allowing it to hit Raging Bolt and Tera Poison Landorus.

  • Assault Vest allows Okidogi to survive special attacks such as Life Orb Ursaluna-B's Tera Normal Blood Moon or Earth Power. Assault Vest also turns offensive Raging Bolt's Thunderbolt and Choice Specs Gholdengo's Shadow Ball into 3HKOs.

  • This EV spread allows Okidogi to OHKO Rillaboom with Gunk Shot, OHKO bulkier Landorus variants with Ice Punch, OHKO bulkless Ogerpon-H with Poison Jab, and 2HKO offensive Raging Bolt with High Horsepower. The Speed lets Okidogi outspeed Jolly Chien-Pao in Tailwind and most Raging Bolt.

  • Both Tera Water and Dragon give Okidogi resistances to Water-type attacks such as Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and Fire-type attacks such as Ogerpon-H's Ivy Cudgel while removing Okidogi's Psychic and Ground weaknesses. Tera Water does not give Okidogi weaknesses to Fairy-type attacks such as Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Dazzling Gleam, but it does make Okidogi weak to Grass-type attacks such as Rillaboom's Wood Hammer and Ogerpon-W's Horn Leech. Tera Dragon has the benefit of not making Okidogi weak to Grass, unlike Tera Water, allowing Okidogi to beat Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-W.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 7-9 points

Overview: Okidogi is a solid budget option that primarily fulfils an offensive role with its high Attack and decent bulk, especially on the physical side. With access to powerful moves such as Gunk Shot and Close Combat, only a few Pokemon can switch in safely against it. Toxic Chain lets Okidogi spread status to foes that can be poisoned, and Guard Dog prevents Pokemon with Intimidate from checking it reliably. However, it suffers from having a poor Speed tier, requiring careful positioning, and having competition from other mid-tier Fighting-types that offer higher Speed and pivoting, leaving it regularly undrafted.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Wallbreaker: Okidogi can utilize Choice Band to deal a devastating amount of damage to threats in matches where it may not find the opportunity to set up. Its low Speed, however, makes it vulnerable to revenge killers, forcing it to often switch out after committing to a move.

Speed Control: Okidogi can don a Choice Scarf to threaten faster offensive threats. This set works especially well combined with Toxic Chain to cripple opposing defensive pieces and allow its partners to clean up late-game.

Setup Sweeper: Okidogi can utilize Bulk Up to turn into a deadly late-game cleaner. This set can be run with Drain Punch to increase longevity.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Close Combat, Drain Punch, Body Press, Gunk Shot, Poison Jab

Setup Moves: Bulk Up

Utility Moves: Taunt, Substitute, Brick Break, Roar

Coverage: Knock Off, Psychic Fangs, High Horsepower, Stomping Tantrum, Ice Punch, Thunder Punch, Fire Punch

Niche Moves

Substitute: Substitute is useful on Bulk Up sets where Okidogi can utilize its STAB attacks most effectively against opposing teams and become a more powerful late-game cleaner.

Toxic: Although Toxic Chain is more frequently used to poison foes, Okidogi can use Toxic to guarantee intoxicating defensive walls and pivots to gain progress in a game and help its offensive teammates wallbreak.

Counter: By investing in bulk, Okidogi can survive powerful moves inflicted on it and KO an opposing threat with Counter. This is very prediction reliant, however, as a single turn could be wasted with the foe setting up, allowing them to get ahead in the game.

Common Items

Choice Band: Choice Band maximizes Okidogi's Attack output to punch holes on the opposing team.

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf increases Okidogi's Speed to get the jump on faster threats and revenge kill them.

Leftovers: Leftovers give Okidogi passive recovery for Bulk Up sets, turning it into a potent late-game sweeper if not dealt with quickly.

Resistance Berry: Resistance Berries allow Okidogi to survive strong super effective hits and fire back with one of its powerful STAB attacks or remove an important item with Knock Off.

Niche Items

Mental Herb: Mental Herb can be useful to prevent Okidogi from being interrupted while setting up with Bulk Up, gaining a crucial boost.

Assault Vest: Assault Vest can be used alongside Okidogi's decent coverage to increase its less impressive Special Defense to stay around longer in a match.

Rocky Helmet: Donning a Rocky Helmet allows Okidogi to leverage its physical bulk and punish common pivoting moves such as U-turn and Flip Turn. It is also able to take on a flurry of priority moves such as Aqua Jet and Sucker Punch.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Okidogi can run Heavy-Duty Boots to get around Spikes and enter the field more frequently throughout a match.

Tera

Okidogi is a suitable low-tier Tera Captain option to consider for your draft. Tera Dark is the most common, since it invalidates Okidogi's major to Psychic, gives Knock Off a damage boost, and threatens opposing Ghost-types. Tera Poison or Fighting are particularly useful to boost Okidogi's existing STAB moves further, and Tera Flying removes its Ground weakness to gain a turn by either setting up or punching holes on a would-be check.

Draft Strategy

Okidogi should generally be drafted to provide offensive pressure alongside faster, frailer partners such as Greninja and Meowscarada. Its ability to threaten opponents with Toxic Chain should not go unnoticed, forcing defensive preparations that could limit damage output from the opposing team.

Entry Hazard Support: Okidogi greatly appreciates Spikes and Stealth Rock to punish would-be checks that fall victim to its Toxic Chain ability. Choice Band sets with this support can KO opposing threats and cripple defensive pieces to the point that they are no longer able to switch in reliably. Sticky Web also provides a massive opportunity for it to use Bulk Up more reliably against faster threats. Okidogi appreciates having Ting-Lu as a partner to deal with opposing Ghost- and Poison-types that otherwise wall it, but other entry hazard setters like Iron Treads and Hisuian Samurott are effective.

Fast Pivots: Okidogi can use its impressive physical bulk to tank hits, allowing fast pivots like Greninja and Meowscarada to safely pivot to it. This can provide great opportunities for it to punch holes in opposing threats and allow revenge killers to finish off late-game.

Special Wallbreakers: Okidogi can lure in physically defensive threats to allow special wallbreakers such as Chi-Yu, Latios, and Darkrai to cripple them throughout the course of the game. These teammates also appreciate foes taking damage over time from Okidogi's Toxic Chain.

Checks and Counters

Poison- and Ghost-types: Okidogi's STAB combination is resisted by both Poison- and Ghost-types, with Poison-types also being immune to Toxic Chain. While Okidogi has coverage to handle most of its checks, Pokemon such as Gholdengo can reliably switch in and prey on its lower Special Defense, forcing it out.

Faster Offensive Pokemon: Against faster threats such as Great Tusk, Iron Boulder, and Tornadus-T, Okidogi is heavily limited in its role as a physically offensive wallbreaker, often having to rely on Choice Scarf to make some sort of progress, and it can easily be revenged killed by the aforementioned foes.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Okidogi struggles to make progress against physically bulky Pokemon, which may also use Rocky Helmet to slowly whittle it down. This is especially dangerous, as almost all of Okidogi's moves make contact. Examples of these checks include Alomomola and Skarmory.

movesets.name: Bulk Up (Poison)
movesets.description: Okidogi serves Poison teams as a valuable win condition thanks to Bulk Up enabling it to crush types such as Steel and Dark late-game. Drain Punch enables Okidogi to stay healthy while dealing with threats such as Ting-Lu, Bisharp, and Heatran. Knock Off provides solid coverage, hitting Psychic- and Ghost-types like Galarian Slowking and Mega Sableye along with removing annoying held items like Skarmory's Rocky Helmet. Substitute allows Okidogi to safely set up in front of threats such as Sableye and Hisuian Goodra. The first EV spread enables Okidogi to outspeed Jolly Ursaluna and Modest Magnezone while maximizing its special bulk to comfortably take on the likes of Heatran and Kyurem; it also lets Okidogi survive Choice Band Excadrill's Earthquake after a Bulk Up. The second set trades a bit of special bulk while enabling it to outspeed Adamant Bisharp and Modest Volcanion. Alolan Muk is an essential teammate, being able to remove the Psychic- and Ghost-types that majorly threaten Okidogi such as Tapu Lele, Alolan Raichu, and Blacephalon. Toxapex can handle physical attackers such as Mega Scizor, Cinderace, and Barraskewda along with being able to burn foes with Scald, enabling Okidogi to easily set up on physical attackers like Ting-Lu and Corviknight. Mega Venusaur provides Leech Seed support to give Okidogi an easier time getting in and setting up along with handling Ground- and Water-types like Landorus-T, Mamoswine, and Urshifu-R. Galarian Slowking can set Future Sight to pressure checks such as Great Tusk and can bring Okidogi in safely with Chilly Reception. Choice Scarf Nihilego provides incredible speed control, being able to check threats like Tornadus-T, Volcarona, and Kommo-o along with removing Landorus with Hidden Power Ice. Nidoking can obliterate the physically defensive walls wishing to take on Okidogi such as Iron Defense Skarmory, Pecharunt, and Gliscor and in return appreciates Okidogi removing special walls like Blissey and Ting-Lu.
